passage:
Play centre note, Saturday morning.
Samir (5) and his sister Sofia (3) were at the block corner. Their father sat nearby on his phone. Sofia built a tall tower. Samir watched her, then watched his father. He swept the tower over with one hand. Then he looked straight at his father. His father looked up and said, "Samir, why?" Samir shrugged. He didn't know.
I asked Samir to help me build a bigger tower with Sofia. He did.
— Francis, play centre staff

qa.q: Who built the tall tower?
qa.a: Sofia built the tall tower.

qa.q: What did Samir want when he looked straight at his father?
qa.a: He seemed to feel ignored and wanted his father's attention, even if it meant getting told off.

qa.q: What could Samir's father try next time?
qa.a: He could put the phone away and notice Samir before trouble starts, like playing blocks with both children.

qa.q: How might Sofia feel when her tower falls?
qa.a: She probably feels upset and confused, since she was only building and her brother knocked it over. 😢

grounding: It shows a boy knocking over his sister's blocks and watching to see if a parent looks at him, not knowing himself why he did it.

passage: In the mud courtyard of their house, Tanvir's sister Damini was stacking small clay pots into a tower. Amma sat nearby, sorting rice. Tanvir, five, sat on the step, watching Amma, who did not look up. He walked over and kicked the tower. The pots rolled everywhere. Damini shrieked. Tanvir looked at Amma. Now Amma looked. "Tanvir! What did you do that for?" Tanvir stood there, scratching his leg. He did not know what to say. He just looked at Amma.

qa.q: What was Damini stacking into a tower?
qa.a: She was stacking small clay pots into a tower.

qa.q: What did Tanvir want when he kicked the tower?
qa.a: He felt ignored and wanted Amma to look at him, because she had been busy and not noticing him.

qa.q: What could Amma do to break this pattern?
qa.a: She could give Tanvir small moments of attention when he is calm, like sitting him beside her while she sorts rice, so he doesn't need trouble to be noticed.

qa.q: What is it like for Damini when her pots roll everywhere?
qa.a: She is upset and shocked, shrieking because her careful tower was ruined for no reason she can see.

grounding: It illustrates a boy knocking over his sister's tower and watching whether his mother will look, where even a scolding is attention.

passage:
The power had gone, and Amma was cooking by the light of a lantern, on the phone at the same time.

On the floor, his sister Kiran had built a tall tower of wooden blocks. Kishore sat nearby with nothing to do. He called, "Amma, look!" and hopped on one foot. Amma didn't turn around.

He crawled over and pushed Kiran's tower with one finger. It crashed down.

Kiran screamed.

Amma spun around. "Kishore! Why did you do that?"

Kishore looked at the scattered blocks, then at Amma, who was finally looking at him. He didn't know why. He just knew she was looking now.

qa.q: How was Amma cooking?
qa.a: By the light of a lantern.

qa.q: Why did Kishore push over Kiran's tower?
qa.a: He felt ignored while Amma was busy, and even being scolded meant Amma would look at him.

qa.q: What small step could help Kishore next time?
qa.a: Amma could give Kishore a small job or a quick hug when she's busy, so he gets attention without knocking things over.

qa.q: How does Kiran feel when her tower crashes?
qa.a: She feels upset and angry, which is why she screams.

grounding: During a power cut, Kishore knocks over his sister's tower to make his busy mother look at him, not really knowing why he did it.

passage:
On Sunday morning in their Ludhiana flat, Gargi was building a castle with her blocks on the living room rug. Mummy sat beside her, clapping at every new tower.

Amandeep was across the room with his toy car. Nobody clapped for his car.

He drove it slowly towards the rug. Mummy was still watching Gargi.

He drove the car straight into the castle. Blocks flew everywhere.

Gargi burst into tears. Mummy's head snapped round. "Amandeep! Why?"

Amandeep stared at her. He didn't know why. He just knew that for a moment, Mummy was looking only at him.

qa.q: What was Gargi building?
qa.a: A castle with her blocks.

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling before he crashed into the castle?
qa.a: He felt left out, watching Mummy clap for Gargi while nobody clapped for his car.

qa.q: What could Mummy try next time?
qa.a: Notice Amandeep too, maybe clapping for his car or inviting him to build with Gargi, so he doesn't need to knock things down to be seen.

qa.q: How did Gargi react when her castle was destroyed?
qa.a: She burst into tears, feeling hurt and upset.

grounding: Amandeep drives his car into his sister's block castle to make his mother look at him, preferring a scolding to being unseen.

passage:
"Mumma, look at my tower!"

"Beautiful, Bidisha! So tall!"

"Mumma, look at me jumping!"

"One minute, Sahil. Bidisha, add a red one on top."

"Mumma, look!"

"Sahil, wait."

Crash.

"MUMMA! Sahil broke my tower!"

"Sahil! Why did you do that?"

"..."

"Say sorry to your sister."

"..."

"Sahil, why?"

"I don't know."

"You must know."

"I don't. You were looking at her."

qa.q: What did Sahil want Mumma to look at?
qa.a: Him jumping.

qa.q: What does Sahil's "You were looking at her" reveal?
qa.a: It reveals Sahil felt left out and wanted Mumma's attention, even at the cost of getting into trouble.

qa.q: How could Mumma respond now?
qa.a: Kneel down, acknowledge that Sahil wanted her to look at him too, and then help both children rebuild the tower.

qa.q: How does Bidisha feel when her tower falls?
qa.a: She feels upset and angry, shouting for Mumma.

grounding: In dialogue Sahil knocks down his sister's tower when Mumma keeps looking at her, not knowing why beyond wanting to be seen.

passage: Note for Mr and Mrs Menon, from the afternoon sitter, Thursday. At four, I was helping Rekha build a block tower on the rug. Akash, colouring at the table, called out twice, "Look at mine!" Each time I said, "In a minute." Then he swept the tower down and turned straight to look at me, not at Rekha. Rekha cried. When I asked why, Akash shrugged: "I don't know." I think any look felt better than none. I comforted Rekha, then sat with Akash and properly admired his colouring. He calmed at once. Perhaps he needs a little one-to-one time around four.

qa.q: What did Akash call out twice from the table?
qa.a: He called out, "Look at mine!"

qa.q: What did Akash want when he looked at the sitter after knocking down the tower?
qa.a: He felt left out and wanted attention; even a cross look felt better than being ignored.

qa.q: What small change could prevent the next knocked-down tower?
qa.a: Giving Akash a little one-to-one time around four, and looking at his work when he asks, before he feels invisible.

qa.q: What is it like for Rekha when her tower is swept down?
qa.a: Rekha is shocked and upset, crying as her careful tower falls for no reason she can see.

grounding: Shows a young child knocking over his sister's blocks to win a grown-up's attention, even a cross one, without knowing why he did it.
